title: The HTTP shim gives Swift's own refusals the network's error, so only words tell them apart
evidence: EngineNatives.swift request() answers a request it will not send (its allow-list: "This app does not send that request.", or no token: "Not signed in.") through the same done(0, ..., why) callback a URLSession failure uses, and shim.ts shimFetch rejects every such answer as new TypeError(why). So cloud-adapters.ts eraseFailure (S50b, PR 1751) tells a refusal from a network outage only by matching those words (NATIVE_REFUSALS), and a token refresh's outage only by Swift's "did not answer." (OAuthClient.post's catch, via CloudSync.accessToken). A reworded Swift string would read a refusal as transient and hold Disconnect. Fix: Swift passes a marker (a status text or code) for its own refusals and for a token outage, the shim rejects with its own error name, and eraseFailure reads the name; keep the words as the fallback for builds 11-13, which never send the marker.
